summary: The note describes how composting is growing as a complement to traditional recycling in local communities, driven by grassroots advocates, municipal programs, businesses, educators, technology and community drives. It cites EPA data showing food scraps and yard trimmings make up over 30% of the US waste stream, and notes challenges such as cost, convenience, contamination and odors.
one_line: Composting is rising alongside recycling through grassroots groups, city programs, businesses, education and technology, driven by data showing organic waste is over 30% of US waste.
key_facts: Since September 2023, a shift in consumer habits has been observed, with many embracing composting as a lifestyle commitment.
Susan Rodriguez and Jonathan Lee are local environmental enthusiasts leading a grassroots composting movement; Rodriguez says "Composting is the next logical step."
A study released on November 15, 2023, by the Environmental Protection Agency found yard trimmings and food scraps together made up over 30% of the United States' waste stream.
Most of that organic waste was primarily ending up in landfills or incinerators.
Waste management consultant Michael Thompson's analysis says that if every household composted, overall waste volume could fall by as much as 24%.

Boulder, Greensboro, and Asheville have integrated composting into their recycling programs since late 2023, with curbside pickup of organic waste delivering material to centrally managed composting facilities.
Alicia Kim, Boulder's Waste Management Director, says every ton of compost produced is a ton of waste diverted from the landfill and a boost for local agriculture.
Municipal programs face challenges including initial resistance over cost and convenience, keeping waste streams free of contamination, and managing odors at composting sites.
Ernie's Café and Lillian's Supermarket have made composting a core part of operations since December 2023; they compost scraps, donate organic waste and educate consumers.
Karen Smith, a sustainability coordinator with the non-profit Green Future, has run educational workshops since early autumn of 2023, including one at a local library.
Apps launched after September 2023 give composting tutorials, remind users when to turn piles or add materials, and connect them with nearby composting facilities.
Availability of compact, odor-free indoor composters has surged, serving urban dwellers with limited space, and manufacturers of home composting products report a boom.
Community gardens and environmental clubs accept organic waste from residents and have started organizing 'compost drives' similar to traditional recycling efforts.
